doc.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999

title: Eastman had no jazz program; first African American in the Philharmonic
summary: Eastman recognized jazz but did not teach it; Carter was the first African American in the Eastman Philharmonic and first bassist in the student ensemble.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: How about at Eastman? Was there a recognized jazz program at Eastman when you were there?
No. They recognized the music but didn’t have a program.
But you were playing bass in the orchestra.

In the Eastman Philharmonic I was the first African American in the orchestra, and when they put together what’s now known as the Eastman Philharmonic School Ensemble, it was composed of the better players of the school at that time, that would be my last year, ’58, ’59; and when they put together the first student ensemble I was the first bassist in that orchestra. No, but jazz wasn’t recognized, it really wasn’t taught as part of the school academic program.
